frontend.prompt:
Scope: Implement only the frontend behavior and UX necessary so the client-side enforces and gracefully handles the access rules and API responses described below. Do not change or assume any backend contracts beyond the explicit facts listed in “API/contract facts”. Do not invent endpoints or additional backend behavior.

API/contract facts the frontend must preserve and rely on (do not omit):
- Superuser may READ other users' resources (GET succeeds for other users' entries).
- PUT and DELETE attempts by a superuser on another user's resource will return HTTP 403 with response body containing detail == "Read-only access".
- Superuser may PUT/DELETE and otherwise write their OWN resources (i.e., entries where owner_id == current user id) normally (PUT/DELETE succeed).
- Normal (non-superuser) users attempting to access other users' resources will receive HTTP 404 for those GETs.
- Any request for a non-existent resource returns HTTP 404.
- When creating a resource, the owner_id must be the current authenticated user (the backend will continue to enforce that owner_id of a created resource equals current user). The frontend must not attempt to assign some other user as owner.

Frontend prerequisites / data available in UI runtime (explicit requirements):
- The frontend must have the authenticated user identity and role available in runtime for decision-making (e.g., currentUser.id and currentUser.is_superuser). If this is not currently available to the frontend, update the auth/session layer so these values are exposed to UI code.
- The GET resource response the frontend consumes must include a reliable ownership indicator (one of these two must be available):
  - entry.owner_id (preferred), or
  - entry.is_owner (boolean)
  If neither is present in the current API response payloads, the frontend implementation must request that the API return owner_id or is_owner for GET resource responses. The frontend MUST NOT guess ownership from other fields.

UI / UX rules to implement:
1) Read vs edit mode determination
- On loading a resource detail view, determine isOwner by comparing entry.owner_id === currentUser.id, or use entry.is_owner if provided.
- Determine isEditable = isOwner (true) OR (isOwner false AND ???). Do not attempt to make other-user entries editable. In short: only entries where isOwner === true are editable in the frontend.
- Additionally, for superusers: they may view others' entries (read-only) but must NOT see edit/delete controls when viewing an entry they do not own.

2) List / index view
- For each item row, show a “View” action for all items the user can GET (superusers: all readable items; normal users: only their visible items per API). Do not assume visibility beyond GET results.
- Show “Edit” and “Delete” actions only when entry.owner_id === currentUser.id. For superusers this means Edit/Delete appear only for items where owner_id == currentUser.id.
- Do not display Edit/Delete for items that the user cannot edit. Do not rely on role alone to show controls.

3) Detail / edit page behavior
- Default to a read-only view when the entry is not owned by the current user (isOwner === false). Render all form fields as read-only (disabled inputs or static text) and hide Edit and Delete controls. Show a persistent non-modal informational banner: "Read-only access: you cannot modify this entry" (or display the backend-provided detail string if you receive it on a PUT/DELETE attempt; see error handling below).
- If isOwner === true, show editable form controls and Edit/Save/Delete actions per normal flow.

4) Create (POST) behavior
- When creating a new resource, the frontend must not attempt to set owner_id to any value other than the currentUser.id. Preferred approach: omit owner_id from POST body entirely, letting the backend set it server-side. If the frontend constructs owner data, explicitly set owner_id = currentUser.id before sending.
- Disable or remove any UI that allows selecting/changing owner at creation time.

5) PUT/DELETE request handling and robust error handling
- For PUT and DELETE requests, implement the following error handling rules:
  a) If response.status === 403 and response.body.detail === "Read-only access":
     - Interpret this as a server-declared read-only constraint for this resource (i.e., it's owned by another user).
     - Immediately revert any optimistic UI changes and stop any retry attempts.
     - Switch the detail view into read-only mode: disable form fields, hide/disable Edit/Delete buttons, and display a clear user-facing message containing the detail text (exactly as returned by the server) or a localized equivalent. Example: banner text = response.body.detail.
     - Log this event for telemetry/diagnostics.
  b) If response.status === 404 on GET: treat as "Not found" and show the Not Found page/UI state. Do not attempt to show read-only content.
  c) If response.status === 404 on PUT/DELETE: the resource does not exist; display Not Found and do not retry.
  d) For other error statuses, follow existing global error handling patterns but avoid changing read-only state unless you receive the explicit 403 + detail above.

6) Direct URL / deep-link / race conditions
- Users may attempt to navigate directly to an edit URL for a resource they do not own. The frontend must not rely solely on route-level guards. Always confirm ownership from the GET resource response before enabling editing on the edit page.
- If a user navigates to an "edit" route and the GET result indicates isOwner === false, redirect or render a read-only view, do not render an editable form.

7) Optimistic updates and rollbacks
- If you perform optimistic updates for PUT/DELETE, be prepared to rollback on 403/404. For 403 with detail == "Read-only access", rollback and switch to read-only mode as described above.

8) Visual cues and copy
- For read-only presentations of other users' entries, show a visible banner/info line: "Read-only: you cannot modify this entry". If a 403 response is received containing detail == "Read-only access", show that exact message in the UI.
- For Not Found cases (404): show standard Not Found UX; do not display any resource content.

9) Form controls and accessibility
- Use disabled attributes for inputs or render static read-only components so screen readers and keyboard users get the correct affordance.
- Ensure focus management when switching from editable to read-only after receiving a 403 (announce the state change via ARIA live region or move focus to the banner).

10) Security / client-side enforcement caveat
- The frontend must enforce these display and control rules only for user experience. Do not rely on the frontend for access control. If a backend returns 403/404 unexpectedly, the frontend must handle it gracefully per the rules above.

Acceptance test checklist (frontend responsibilities):
- Superuser viewing another user's entry: GET succeeds and UI is read-only (no edit/delete); attempting PUT/DELETE triggers 403 with detail == "Read-only access" and the frontend shows the detail and switches to read-only.
- Superuser editing their own entry: GET shows isOwner === true, UI allows editing, PUT/DELETE succeed and UI reflects changes.
- Normal user viewing another user's entry: GET returns 404 and frontend shows Not Found.
- Requesting a non-existent resource: GET returns 404 and frontend shows Not Found.
- Creating a resource: POST omits owner_id or sets owner_id === currentUser.id; created resource (when re-fetched) shows owner_id === currentUser.id or entry.is_owner === true.

Implementation checklist for engineers (concrete steps):
1) Ensure currentUser (id and is_superuser) is available in the UI context.
2) Ensure GET resource payload includes owner_id or is_owner. If not present, stop and request backend change; do not guess ownership.
3) Update list and detail templates/components to compute isOwner from owner_id/is_owner and currentUser.id.
4) Hide/disable Edit/Delete UI for entries where isOwner === false.
5) For detail view, default to read-only when isOwner === false; show read-only banner.
6) On PUT/DELETE failure, inspect response.status and response.body.detail; if 403 && detail === "Read-only access": rollback, switch to read-only, show the returned detail text to the user, and disable further edit attempts.
7) For 404 responses on GET/PUT/DELETE: route to Not Found UI and do not display resource content.
8) Ensure POST body does not allow arbitrary owner_id: omit owner_id or set owner_id = currentUser.id before sending.
9) Add tests (unit/integration) that simulate the above responses and assert the UI states and messages.

Notes and constraints for the frontend implementer (explicit reminders):
- Do not assume the backend will provide any other error text than the exact detail string for READ-ONLY errors: must check for detail === "Read-only access" (string match) when applying the special read-only handling.
- Do not attempt to edit or delete items that the UI determined are not owned by the current user; but still handle server-side 403/404 gracefully in case of race conditions or inconsistent state.
- Do not attempt to circumvent the backend enforcement by sending owner_id other than currentUser.id during create; the frontend must prevent UI-level owner selection.

Deliverables for frontend QA/developers:
- Updated list/detail/create/edit/delete UI implementing the rules above.
- Automated tests covering: superuser own vs other entries, normal user other-entry 404, create owner_id behavior, 403 handling with detail == "Read-only access", and 404 handling.
- A short README note in the frontend repo describing the dependency on the GET payload including owner_id or is_owner and the required currentUser fields.

backend.prompt:
实施范围说明（决定自需求）：
- 资源路径（REST 风格）：
  - 列表/创建: GET /items/ , POST /items/
  - 详情/修改/删除: GET /items/{id}/ , PUT /items/{id}/ , PATCH /items/{id}/ , DELETE /items/{id}/
- 认证：所有端点必须要求已认证用户；未认证返回 401（标准行为）。当前用户从认证上下文获得（not from请求体）。
- 数据模型假定存在 owner_id 字段指向用户标识符。

必须实现的业务规则（逐项明确、不可省略）：
1) 读取权限
   - 超级用户（is_superuser==true）可以读取（GET 列表与 GET 详情）任何用户的条目。
   - 普通用户仅能读取其自身拥有的条目（列表返回仅包括其 own items，详情访问其他人条目应表现为不可见，见写权限一条）。
2) 写权限（PUT / PATCH / DELETE）
   - 条目的拥有者（object.owner_id == current_user.id）可执行 PUT/PATCH/DELETE（写操作允许）。
   - 超级用户对非本人条目：禁止写。对尝试 PUT/PATCH/DELETE 他人条目必须返回 HTTP 403，响应体 JSON 必须为 {"detail": "Read-only access"}（exact 字符串，包含双引号内的内容）。
   - 普通用户对非本人条目：必须表现为资源不存在 —— 返回 HTTP 404（不要返回 403；客户端不得能区分这是因无权限还是不存在）。
3) 非存在资源：任何对不存在 id 的访问（GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE）必须返回 HTTP 404（标准 Not Found 行为）。
4) 创建（POST /items/）
   - 创建时忽略请求体中可能提供的 owner_id 字段；后端必须将新资源的 owner_id 强制设为当前 authenticated user 的 id（current_user.id）。
   - 成功创建返回 HTTP 201（并返回新资源数据，包含 owner_id 为当前用户）。
5) 响应内容与前端协作
   - 为便于前端使“他人条目只读”，在每个 GET（列表项与详情）响应的资源对象中添加一个只读/可编辑标识字段，例如 "editable": true/false 或等价布尔字段。计算逻辑： editable == (object.owner_id == current_user.id)。（可选替代：如果不愿修改 payload，则前端可根据返回的 owner_id 与当前用户 id 决定；但建议提供 editable 以减少前端查用户 id 的需要。）

实现细节（伪代码/步骤，针对任意后端框架可直接转译）
1) 统一获取当前用户
   - current_user = get_authenticated_user_from_request(request)
   - is_superuser = current_user.is_superuser
   - 如果未认证则立即返回 401
2) 列表 GET /items/
   - if is_superuser: queryset = Items.objects.all()
   - else: queryset = Items.objects.filter(owner_id=current_user.id)
   - 在序列化每个对象时附加 editable 字段（editable = object.owner_id == current_user.id）
   - 返回 HTTP 200 与序列化列表
3) 详情 GET /items/{id}/
   - obj = Items.get_by_id(id)
   - if obj == null: return 404
   - // 读权限
   - if is_superuser or obj.owner_id == current_user.id:
       - 构建响应 JSON，包含 editable 字段（editable = obj.owner_id == current_user.id）
       - return 200
     else:
       - 对于普通用户访问他人详情，按规则应返回 404（不可透露存在）
       - return 404
4) 更新 PUT/PATCH /items/{id}/
   - obj = Items.get_by_id(id)
   - if obj == null: return 404
   - if obj.owner_id == current_user.id:
       - 允许更新：应用验证，保存修改，返回 200（或按既有 API 规范返回更新后的资源）
   - else: // 请求目标非本人
       - if is_superuser:
           - return 403 with body {"detail": "Read-only access"}
       - else:
           - return 404
5) 删除 DELETE /items/{id}/
   - obj = Items.get_by_id(id)
   - if obj == null: return 404
   - if obj.owner_id == current_user.id:
       - 执行删除，返回 204 No Content
   - else:
       - if is_superuser:
           - return 403 with body {"detail": "Read-only access"}
       - else:
           - return 404
6) 创建 POST /items/
   - current_user 必须已认证
   - 在创建代码中忽略输入里的 owner_id（如果存在），强制设置 new.owner_id = current_user.id
   - 保存并返回 201 与新对象表示（包含 owner_id=current_user.id 与 editable=true）

错误响应格式化要求（必须精确遵守验收）：
- PUT/PATCH/DELETE 被超级用户对他人条目拒绝时：HTTP 403, 响应 body 必须是 JSON 对象且包含键 detail，值精确为字符串 Read-only access，示例： {"detail": "Read-only access"}
- 任意请求命中“不可见/不存在”情形时：HTTP 404（响应体可为标准 {"detail":"Not found."} 或框架默认 404 格式，但必须是 404 状态码）
- 未认证：HTTP 401（框架标准格式）

测试与验收用例（必须覆盖，自动化）——每项都要通过：
- 超级用户 GET 其他用户条目 -> 200, 返回资源
- 超级用户 PUT 其他用户条目 -> 403, body == {"detail":"Read-only access"}
- 超级用户 DELETE 其他用户条目 -> 403, body == {"detail":"Read-only access"}
- 超级用户 对本人条目 PUT/DELETE -> 成功（200/204，如既有 API 规范）
- 普通用户 GET 自己条目 -> 200
- 普通用户 GET 他人条目 -> 404
- 普通用户 PUT/PATCH/DELETE 他人条目 -> 404
- 普通用户 PUT/DELETE 自己条目 -> 成功（200/204）
- 访问不存在 id 的任何方法 -> 404
- POST 创建时即便请求体包含 owner_id，也必须在数据库里创建为当前用户 id，返回资源 owner_id == current_user.id

实现注意事项与防坑提示：
- 在实现 PUT/PATCH/DELETE 的权限判断时，先查询对象存在性（否则返回 404），再根据 owner 与 is_superuser 判定返回 403 或 404（按规则：超级用户非本人 -> 403；普通用户非本人 -> 404）。
- 不要把超级用户的写入权限泛化为“超级用户可以修改任何资源”——明确按需求阻止超级用户修改他人条目并返回特定的 403 文本。
- 创建时必须保证原子性地覆盖 owner_id，即使客户端并发发送 owner_id 覆盖请求也要以认证用户为准。
- 请把用于前端显示的 editable 字段放入序列化/输出层（不要把其持久化到数据库）。

向已有代码库集成建议（针对常见框架的实现思路）：
- Django REST Framework：实现自定义 Permission 类或在 ViewSet 的 get_object() / perform_update()/perform_destroy() 中加入上述逻辑；在 perform_create() 里强制设置 serializer.save(owner=self.request.user)；在 serializer.to_representation() 添加 editable 字段或在 ViewSet 的 list/retrieve 的序列化上下文中注入并返回。
- Express/Node：在路由中间件中实现认证与 current_user，按步骤在 handlers 中查询对象、判断 owner 与 is_superuser 并返回相应状态码与 JSON。
- 任何框架：保持局部逻辑一致（查询存在 -> 判断 owner/is_superuser -> 按表述返回 404/403/成功），并在序列化输出加入 editable 标志以便前端只读显示。

交付清单（实现完成后交付以供验收）：
- 后端代码变更（列出修改文件）
- 自动化测试用例（覆盖上面列出的场景）
- API 文档更新：明确说明 403 的精确返回体 {"detail":"Read-only access"} 以及创建时 owner_id 被覆盖为当前用户的行为

注意：以上实现说明仅限后端部分。前端需要根据 GET 返回的 editable 字段或 owner_id 与当前用户信息决定是否将表单/按钮置为只读，但前端不可依赖隐藏的服务器侧访问控制——服务器必须按以上规则永远强制返回正确的 403/404。
